description: R11-OKF02 / R11-FP13 retrieval-only corpus for scripts/okf_context_benchmark.py: given a question, does the stored OKF knowledge bundle put the right object in front of the model? It measures aida.okf_context's lexical ranking and assembly and nothing about answer quality -- no model is asked anything. Each case names its expected objects in the corpus vocabulary of footprint_enrichment_corpus.json (TABLE, ROUTINE, ONTOLOGY_CONCEPT, GOVERNED_TOOL; a view or materialized view is a TABLE). `expected` is any-of for the headline hit; `complete` in the report is all-of. `expected_status` is a first-class verdict: NO_MATCH cases carry no object because the bundle holds nothing on the question, and a case with neither an object nor an explicit NO_MATCH is refused by the loader. `forbidden` objects must not be delivered (a gap). `exactly_one_answer` says one object is the right answer, so an AMBIGUOUS status on it is a false ambiguity; `expect_ambiguous` says two objects are equally right and AMBIGUOUS is the correct response. Cases marked `reuse` take their question and expected object from the named case of another corpus at load time, so those two files cannot drift from this one unnoticed; provenance is printed with each result. AUTHORSHIP, STATED PLAINLY: the OWN cases and the `estate` overlay below were written by the same session that read the ranking code, in steward and user voices respectively, and then run once. They are a regression instrument and an ablation illustration -- they show which signal can matter and pin what was measured -- not an estimate of how often production questions are answered. The paraphrase and no_match categories exist so the corpus contains questions a lexical ranker is expected to miss or refuse, and their results are reported as measured. `fixture_only` marks a case whose ground truth exists only in the fixture estate -- approved text the overlay authored (a column meaning, a table description) or an object only the fixture holds (its tool); the API mode skips it, because a stack that does not carry it would score the estate's absence as a ranking miss. Object keys are the harness estate's fixed slugs (ADR-0014); no production data.

estate.note: The harness estate (scripts/quality_benchmark.py: TABLE_SEEDS, FOOTPRINT_ROUTINE_SEEDS, FOOTPRINT_CONCEPT, FOOTPRINT_ROUTINE_DESCRIPTION, TOOL_SEEDS) has tables that carry only a source comment, and a bundle deliberately ignores a source comment -- only an APPROVED Atlas description ranks. So this overlay approves descriptions and column meanings for a subset, the way a steward would, and leaves the rest undescribed: fact_orders, dim_product and dim_employee have no approved table description. Wording is steward-voiced and audited by tests/test_okf_context_benchmark.py so that no overlay text re-creates a lexical path from an enrichment question to its target table.

table_descriptions.dim_customer: One row per retail customer, holding contact details and onboarding attributes.
table_descriptions.fact_payments: One row per completed payment, whatever channel it arrived on.
table_descriptions.dim_branch: One row per bank branch, with its street address and region.
table_descriptions.fact_loan_applications: Every loan application submitted, with the applicant and the decision so far.
table_descriptions.fact_account_balances: A balance for each account on each date, taken from the ledger.
table_descriptions.dim_merchant: The merchants that accept the bank's cards, one row per merchant.
table_descriptions.fact_fraud_alerts: One row per alert the monitoring system has raised, with its severity and how it was resolved.

cases.note: ADDED AFTER THE FIRST RUN, and not authored by this session: it is the question the tracker's own live check of R11-OKF02 asked of the sample estate (2026-09-19), which the walkthrough recorded as answered AMBIGUOUS between two documents. The expected object is the table the sample estate's warehouse schema was built to hold this in. Whether a tie on it is a false ambiguity is exactly what exactly_one_answer asks.
cases.question: Which table holds account balances by date?
How many loan applications were submitted last month?
Which offices does the bank run in each region?
What is a customer's date of birth?
Where is the email address stored?
What will the weather be in Lisbon on Friday?
What is today's EUR to USD exchange rate?

cases.note: ADDED AFTER THE FIRST RUN. The first run of the 25 cases above showed no difference when aliases were removed, because every alias question (`closing position`) also contains `position`, a word of the concept's own name. This case uses only the alias word, so the alias ablation has something to remove. It illustrates the mechanism; it was written after seeing that result and is reported as such.
cases.question: What were the closing numbers?

cases.note: ADDED AFTER THE FIRST RUN. The three no_match cases above share no word with the estate at all, so they could only ever pass. This one shares a word (`customer`) with a real table while asking for something no object holds -- the false match a lexical ranker is prone to. The ground truth is unambiguous: the estate has no satisfaction data.
cases.question: What is our customer satisfaction score?
How much money do customers hold at the end of each day?
